title: Grade 6 Science — Fri, Jun 13
description: Separation of Substances — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — matching methods to mixtures
subject: science

questions.question: Match: To separate stone from rice, use:
questions.explanation: Stones can be seen and picked out by hand. Hand-picking is the simplest method for visible particles in a dry mixture.

questions.question: Match: To separate salt from water, use:
questions.explanation: Salt dissolves in water. To get salt back, heat the solution so water evaporates, leaving solid salt crystals.

questions.question: Match: To separate sand from water, use:
questions.explanation: Sand is insoluble in water. Filtration separates it — sand remains on filter paper while water passes through.

questions.question: Match: To separate iron filings from sawdust, use:
questions.explanation: Iron filings are magnetic; sawdust is not. A magnet can easily pull iron filings away from sawdust.

questions.question: Match: To separate husk from grain, use:
questions.explanation: Winnowing uses wind to blow the lighter husk away while the heavier grain falls and is collected.

questions.question: Match: To get pure water from seawater, use:
questions.explanation: Distillation condenses water vapour into pure water, leaving all dissolved salts behind.

questions.question: Which of these mixtures requires two steps: sedimentation THEN filtration?
questions.explanation: First let the mud settle (sedimentation), then filter the clearer water to remove remaining fine particles.

questions.question: Match: To identify the different dyes in a felt-tip pen ink, use:
questions.explanation: Paper chromatography separates the different coloured dye components in ink by how fast they travel up wet paper.

questions.question: A mixture of flour (fine) and rice (coarse grain) can be separated using:
questions.explanation: A sieve with appropriate hole size lets fine flour through but retains the larger rice grains.

questions.question: Salt water and pure water both look the same. How can we confirm which is which?
options: By evaporating both — salt water leaves a white residue
questions.explanation: Evaporate samples from both. The salt water leaves white salt crystals. Pure water leaves no residue.

questions.question: Which method cannot be used to separate a DISSOLVED substance from water?
questions.explanation: Filtration only removes insoluble (undissolved) particles. A dissolved substance like salt passes right through filter paper.

questions.question: Water treatment plants use a combination of methods. In the correct order, they are:
questions.explanation: Water purification: coagulate + sediment → filter to remove particles → add chlorine to kill germs.

questions.question: The process where vapour turns back to liquid is:
questions.explanation: Condensation is the reverse of evaporation — vapour cools and turns back into liquid. It is used in distillation.

questions.question: When would you use BOTH sieving AND evaporation together?
options: When separating a mixture that has both large particles AND dissolved salt (e.g., salty muddy water)
When finding which materials are magnetic
questions.explanation: Sieve out the large particles, then evaporate to get the dissolved salt. Different impurities need different methods.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to separate two LIQUIDS that mix together (miscible) but have different boiling points?
questions.explanation: Distillation separates miscible liquids with different boiling points by boiling the more volatile one first and condensing it.
